blocks.text: After describing the fear Banda inspired among Mughal officials, the narrative redirects the campaign toward a new terrain. Banda turns toward the hills after consolidating success in Punjab, showing that victory on the plains now authorizes punitive movement against the hill states.

The page links that movement to earlier hostility from Kahloor and Bilaspur and to the accumulated grievances associated with the Guru's struggles there. It also makes clear that punishment will be selective, because those who join the Sikhs can still expect protection rather than indiscriminate devastation.
As a transition page, it closes one cycle of Mughal fear and opens another cycle of regional reckoning. The center of action shifts, but Banda's authority continues to expand.
